description.narrative: The project is implemented in Turkey. The main outcome areas it contributes to are democracy and human rights and peace and dialogue. The main right holders are youth and human rights activists within the civil society organisations that work on peace and peace building.Through trainings, organising and mobilising, advocacy and capacity building the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between Truth, Justice and Memory Center in Turkey, the Swedish Social Democratic Youth League in Gävleborg (SSU-Gävleborg) and the Palme Center.The local partner organisation Truth, Justice and Memory Center works primarily with peace research, dealing with the past and capacity building of the civil societies as peace advocates. The SSU-Gävleborg, one of the Palme Center's member organisations, is highly engaged in the development in Turkey, with a memberbase intrested in contribution to the democratic development. They support this partnership with their specific focus on and expertise in youth advocacy, youth participation and will function as a channel to relevant organisations in Sweden and Europe. The Palme Center will support the project with administrative and technical support.Other Donors to the OrganisationThe local organisation conducts its' operations with donations and funds from EU, but this project is funded only by the Palme Center.Project ObjectiveThe project's objective is to increase the contribution of Turkey s civil society to peace advocacy through research and capacity building to enable the civil society to take a more active role in both supporting the resumption of a new peace process and during a possible new peace process.Actor groupsThe main actor group in the project are civil society organizations that work on peace and peace building and young human rights activists who are eager to participate in peace advocacy and activism.The organisations main actors within the group of, 1) right holders are: women, youth, minorities and the human rights activists in the civil society organisations.2) actors working in cooperation: the civil society organisations in Turkey and international organisations working on human rights and peace building.3) decision makers: the government agencies and the political leadership in the political parties.
